claim.quote: We report on the final electroweak measurements performed with data taken at the Z resonance by the experiments operating at the electron-positron colliders SLC and LEP.

date.note: arXiv submission month (7 Sep 2005); journal publication followed in 2006.

key_value_text.quote: The number of light neutrino species is determined to be 2.9840+/-0.0082.
key_value_text.value: Final combined LEP+SLD Z-pole measurements: Z mass, width, asymmetries and the number of light neutrino species (2.9840+/-0.0082) are all reported to per-mille precision; the abstract as fetched does not restate the Z mass/width numbers themselves.

name: Precision Electroweak Measurements on the Z Resonance
notes: SLD (SLC Large Detector) is one of the five contributing experiments/collaborations in this combination but is outside the scope of this workstream (not a CERN experiment) and is not listed in experiment_ids/collaboration_ids; only the four LEP experiments are recorded here.

summary.plain: The final report card of LEP and its sister collider SLC: after a decade of data, physicists combined every measurement of the Z boson from all five experiments into one definitive set of numbers.
summary.technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and SLD combination, Phys. Rept. 427 (2006) 257-454 (arXiv:hep-ex/0509008); the final electroweak measurements at the Z resonance from LEP and SLC, including the Z mass and width, asymmetries and the number of light neutrino species (2.9840+/-0.0082).

title: Precision Electroweak Measurements on the Z Resonance
why_it_matters: Turned a decade of LEP and SLC running into the definitive precision test of the electroweak Standard Model, constraining the top-quark and Higgs-boson masses before either was directly measured/discovered and setting the benchmark every later collider measurement is checked against.
